Loaded via JOIN with the hrm_members table using the hrm_members_id foreign key. Contains summary information about the member who triggered the logged event. For system-generated actions, this may reference a system service account.
performer.x-autobe-specification: JOIN from hrm_activity_logs.hrm_members_id to hrm_members.id. Returns IHrmMember.ISummary via hrmMember relation.

created_at.description:
When this log entry was created in the database.

Automatically set when the activity log record is inserted. This may differ from the timestamp field if log entries are written asynchronously after the action occurs.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_activity_logs.created_at. DateTime with timestamptz format.

deleted_at.description:
When this log entry was soft-deleted.

Audit logs are typically retained indefinitely, but soft delete support allows for compliance-driven data removal when required. Null value indicates the log entry is active and not deleted.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_activity_logs.deleted_at. DateTime with timestamptz format, nullable.

IHrmActivityLog.ISummary.description:
Activity log summary record for audit trail browsing.

This type represents a summarized activity log entry optimized for paginated list displays in administrative interfaces. Each record captures a significant system event including who performed the action, what type of action it was, when it occurred, and which entity was affected.

**Key Fields**

- id - Unique identifier for the log entry (UUID format)
- timestamp - When the action occurred (ordered descending by default)
- action_type - Category of business event (e.g., employee_invited, contract_created, task_status_changed)
- performer - User who performed the action (loaded via JOIN with hrm_members)
- target_entity_type and target_entity_id - Polymorphic reference to affected entity (nullable for system-wide events)
- details - JSON-formatted contextual information about the action

**Access Control**

Activity logs are organization-scoped. Users can only view logs from organizations they belong to with appropriate permissions (org:manage). Logs are strictly isolated between organizations.
IHrmActivityLog.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_activity_logs table with hrmMember relation JOIN. Columns: id, timestamp, action_type, target_entity_type, target_entity_id, details, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Relation: hrmMember → performer (IHrmMember.ISummary via JOIN on hrm_members_id). Details stored as JSON string. target_entity_id and deleted_at nullable for system-wide events and soft-delete support.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the employment contract record.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the contract entity and is used to reference this specific contract in API operations and database queries.
id.x-autobe-specification: Retrieved from hrm_contracts.id via JOIN. Primary key uniquely identifying the contract record.

organization_id.description:
Unique identifier for the organization that employs this employee.

This UUID identifies the multi-tenant organization context for the contract. All contracts are scoped to a single organization for data isolation and access control purposes.
organization_id.x-autobe-specification: Retrieved from hrm_employees.organization_id via JOIN on hrm_employee_id. Identifies the organization to which this contract belongs.

employee.description:
Summary information about the employee associated with this contract.

Contains essential employee details including position, employment type, and current status within the organization. This reference allows administrators to identify which employee's contract is expiring without loading the full employee record.
employee.x-autobe-specification: JOIN from hrm_contracts.hrm_employee_id to hrm_employees.id. Returns IHrmEmployee.ISummary with position, employment_type, status, and user reference.

start_date.description:
The effective start date of this employment contract.

This timestamp marks when the contractual terms (pay rate, working hours, etc.) become active. The field is required and cannot be null. When creating a new contract, the system validates that the start_date does not overlap with existing active contracts for the same employee.
start_date.x-autobe-specification: Retrieved from hrm_contracts.start_date via JOIN. Required field marking when contractual terms become active.

end_date.description:
The effective end date of this employment contract.

A NULL value indicates the contract is currently active. When a new contract is created for an employee, the previous active contract's end_date is automatically set to one day before the new contract's start_date. Once end_date is populated, the contract becomes immutable to preserve historical accuracy. For expiration reporting, contracts with NULL end_date are treated as having a default 90-day warning period.
end_date.x-autobe-specification: Retrieved from hrm_contracts.end_date via JOIN. Nullable - NULL indicates active contract. Used for expiration calculation.

pay_rate.description:
The compensation rate specified in this contract.

This numeric value represents the pay amount, with the unit determined by the pay_period field (hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly). The value is stored in the organization's base currency and is used for payroll calculations, budget tracking, and employment verification.
pay_rate.x-autobe-specification: Retrieved from hrm_contracts.pay_rate via JOIN. Numeric value in organization's base currency.

pay_period.description:
The frequency at which the pay_rate is applied.

Valid values are:
- hourly: Pay rate per hour worked
- daily: Pay rate per day worked
- weekly: Pay rate per week
- monthly: Pay rate per month

This field determines how the pay_rate value should be interpreted for payroll calculations and budget planning.
pay_period.x-autobe-specification: Retrieved from hrm_contracts.pay_period via JOIN. Enumeration: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly.

working_hours_per_week.description:
The expected number of working hours per week under this contract.

This optional field is used for full-time vs part-time classification, overtime calculations, and compliance with labor regulations. May be null for contractor or irregular work arrangements where hourly tracking is not applicable.
working_hours_per_week.x-autobe-specification: Retrieved from hrm_contracts.working_hours_per_week via JOIN. Nullable - optional for contractor/irregular arrangements.

days_until_expiration.description:
Number of days remaining until the contract expires.

This field is calculated server-side based on the current date and the contract's end_date. For contracts with a set end_date, it shows the exact number of days remaining. For active contracts (end_date IS NULL), it shows the default warning period of 90 days. This value is used to sort contracts by urgency, with the most urgent renewals appearing first.
days_until_expiration.x-autobe-specification: Computed field: days_until_expiration = (end_date - current_date) in days for contracts with end_date. If end_date is NULL (active contract), calculate as 90 days from current date (default warning period). Used for sorting contracts by urgency (ascending).

IHrmContractExpirationSummary.description:
Contract expiration summary report entry showing employment contracts requiring renewal attention.

This type represents a single contract record in the contract expiration report, combining contract details with employee information and calculating days remaining until expiration. It helps organization administrators proactively manage contract renewals and avoid gaps in employment agreements.

**Contract Details**

Includes the contract's start date, end date, pay rate, pay period frequency, and expected working hours per week. The days_until_expiration field is calculated server-side based on the current date and contract end_date.

**Employee Context**

Each entry includes a summary of the associated employee via the employee field, providing their position, employment type, and current status within the organization. This allows administrators to identify which employees have contracts requiring renewal attention.

**Business Rules**

Active contracts (end_date IS NULL) are included with days_until_expiration calculated based on a default warning period of 90 days. Contracts with end_date within the specified range are sorted by expiration date ascending, showing the most urgent renewals first.
IHrmContractExpirationSummary.x-autobe-specification: Computed type: LEFT JOIN hrm_contracts with hrm_employees ON hrm_employee_id. Filter: end_date IS NULL (active contracts) OR end_date within specified date range from query parameters. Calculate days_until_expiration = (end_date - current_date) in days for contracts with end_date; if end_date is NULL, calculate as 90 days from now (default warning period). Include employee summary via JOIN on hrm_employees. organization_id retrieved from hrm_employees.organization_id via JOIN. Sort by end_date ascending (NULLs last) for urgency ordering.

total_count.description:
Total number of employees matching the filter criteria.

This count represents all employees within the authenticated user's organization context that satisfy the applied filter conditions. When no filters are provided in the request, this includes all employees in the organization. The count is computed via COUNT(*) aggregation on the hrm_employees table.
total_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed COUNT(*) of employees matching filter criteria from hrm_employees table with organization context. Returns integer count, zero if no employees match filters.

employment_type_breakdown.description:
Breakdown of employees by employment type (full-time, part-time, contractor, intern).

This array contains distribution statistics showing how many employees fall into each employment type category. Each element includes the employment type identifier and the count of employees with that type. Categories with zero employees are omitted from the array.

**Valid Employment Types**

- full-time: Standard full-time employment
- part-time: Part-time employment arrangement
- contractor: Contract-based employment
- intern: Internship position
employment_type_breakdown.x-autobe-specification: Computed GROUP BY employment_type aggregation from hrm_employees table. Returns array of objects with employment_type value and count. Valid employment types: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern. Empty categories omitted from array.

status_breakdown.description:
Breakdown of employees by status (active, deactivated).

This array contains distribution statistics showing how many employees are in each status state. Each element includes the status identifier and the count of employees with that status. Categories with zero employees are omitted from the array.

**Valid Status Values**

- active: Employee currently employed and active
- deactivated: Employee record exists but employment has ended or is suspended
status_breakdown.x-autobe-specification: Computed GROUP BY status aggregation from hrm_employees table. Returns array of objects with status value and count. Valid statuses: active, deactivated. Empty categories omitted from array.

department_breakdown.description:
Breakdown of employees by department with department names and counts.

This array contains distribution statistics showing how many employees are assigned to each department within the organization. Each element includes the department identifier, department display name, and the count of employees in that department.

**Unassigned Employees**

Employees whose department_id is null are grouped under an 'unassigned' category with a null department_id and the name 'Unassigned'.

**Empty Departments**

Departments with zero employees are omitted from the array.
department_breakdown.x-autobe-specification: Computed GROUP BY department_id aggregation from hrm_employees table with LEFT JOIN to hrm_departments for department names. Returns array of objects with department_id, department_name, and count. Employees with null department_id grouped as 'unassigned' category. Empty categories omitted from array.

role_breakdown.description:
Breakdown of employees by role with role names and counts.

This array contains distribution statistics showing how many employees have each role assignment within the organization. Each element includes the role identifier, role display name, and the count of employees with that role.

**Unassigned Roles**

Employees whose role_id is null are grouped under an 'unassigned' category with a null role_id and the name 'Unassigned'.

**Empty Roles**

Roles with zero employees are omitted from the array.
role_breakdown.x-autobe-specification: Computed GROUP BY role_id aggregation from hrm_employees table with LEFT JOIN to hrm_roles for role names. Returns array of objects with role_id, role_name, and count. Employees with null role_id grouped as 'unassigned' category. Empty categories omitted from array.

IHrmEmployeeAnalytic.description:
Aggregated employee analytics data including total count and distribution breakdowns by employment type, status, department, and role.

This type represents workforce statistics computed from employee records within an organization. It supports filtering by date range, department, employment type, and status to provide targeted analytics for workforce planning and reporting.

**Total Count**

The total_count field represents the number of employees matching the applied filter criteria within the authenticated user's organization context.

**Distribution Breakdowns**

Each breakdown array contains objects with the category identifier, display name (where applicable), and count of employees in that category. Empty categories are omitted from the arrays.

- Employment type breakdown: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern
- Status breakdown: active, deactivated
- Department breakdown: includes department name and employee count per department
- Role breakdown: includes role name and employee count per role

**Filtering**

Analytics can be narrowed using the IHrmEmployeeAnalytic.IRequest filter criteria. When no filters are provided, analytics include all employees within the organization.
IHrmEmployeeAnalytic.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation from hrm_employees table with organization context from authenticated session. Implementation:

1. Query hrm_employees filtered by organization_id from session context
2. Apply optional filters from request body:
   - date_range: filter created_at BETWEEN start AND end
   - department_id: filter department_id = value
   - employment_types: filter employment_type IN array
   - statuses: filter status IN array
3. Perform aggregations:
   - total_count: COUNT(*) of filtered employees
   - employment_type_breakdown: GROUP BY employment_type, COUNT(*) per type
   - status_breakdown: GROUP BY status, COUNT(*) per status
   - department_breakdown: LEFT JOIN hrm_departments ON department_id, GROUP BY department_id, COUNT(*) per department (null department_id grouped as 'unassigned')
   - role_breakdown: LEFT JOIN hrm_roles ON role_id, GROUP BY role_id, COUNT(*) per role
4. Return zero counts for empty result sets
5. Omit empty categories from breakdown arrays

IHrmEmployeeAnalyticIEmploymentTypeBreak.description:
Employment type distribution breakdown entry for employee analytics.

This type represents a single employment type category within the workforce distribution analytics. Each entry contains the employment type identifier and the count of employees assigned to that type.

**Employment Type Values**

period.description:
The time bucket identifier in ISO 8601 format, representing the start of the time period.

This computed field represents the beginning of an aggregated time window (daily, weekly, or monthly). The specific granularity is determined automatically based on the queried date range to provide meaningful visualizations. For example, a 30-day range might use daily buckets, while a 2-year range might use monthly buckets.
period.x-autobe-specification: Computed time bucket identifier. Generated from hrm_activity_logs.timestamp column using time_bucket aggregation function. Format: ISO 8601 datetime representing the start of the time period (day/week/month boundary). Time granularity automatically determined by query date range.

count.description:
The number of activity log entries within this time period.

This computed field contains the total count of activity log records that occurred during the time window represented by the period field. The count reflects all activity types recorded in the system for the specified time bucket, providing insight into activity volume trends over time.
count.x-autobe-specification: Computed COUNT(*) aggregation of hrm_activity_logs records within the time bucket. Integer value representing the number of activity log entries that fall within the period time range.

IHrmActivityLogAnalytic.ITemporalTrend.description:
Temporal activity trend entry representing activity count for a specific time period.

Each entry in the temporal trends array represents a time bucket (day, week, or month) with the corresponding activity count for that period. The time granularity is automatically determined based on the query date range to provide meaningful aggregations.

This DTO is used in activity log analytics endpoints to display time-series data showing how activity volume changes over time. The period field uses ISO 8601 format to represent the start of each time bucket, enabling consistent client-side charting and visualization.
IHrmActivityLogAnalytic.ITemporalTrend.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation from hrm_activity_logs table. Each entry represents a time bucket (daily/weekly/monthly) with activity count. Time buckets computed from timestamp column using time_bucket function, grouped by time period. Returns array of period objects with count. Granularity automatically determined by query date range.

count.description:

count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT(*) aggregation per role_id group. Minimum 1 since empty categories omitted. Computed via GROUP BY role_id with COUNT aggregation.

IHrmEmployeeAnalyticIRoleBreakdown.description:
Role breakdown entry in employee analytics showing role identifier, display name, and employee count.

This type represents a single category in the role distribution breakdown within employee analytics. Each entry contains the role identifier, the role's display name, and the count of employees assigned to that role within the organization.

**Role Identification**

The `role_id` field contains the UUID of the role from the hrm_roles table. For employees without a role assignment (null role_id), this field is null and the role_name is 'Unassigned'.

The `count` field represents the number of employees with this role assignment within the organization, as computed by GROUP BY aggregation. Empty role categories with zero employees are omitted from the result array entirely.

Employees with null role_id are grouped as 'unassigned' category with role_id=null and role_name='Unassigned'. Empty role categories (zero employees) are omitted from the result array.

hours_breakdown.description:
Aggregated time tracking metrics for the project during the reporting week.

Computed from hrm_timelogs records associated with this project. Contains three metrics:

- total_hours: Sum of all timelog durations (in hours) for this project during the week
- billable_hours: Sum of billable timelog durations (in hours) for this project
- non_billable_hours: Difference between total_hours and billable_hours (internal/non-chargeable work)

All values are rounded to reasonable precision for display purposes.
hours_breakdown.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation from hrm_timelogs for the reporting week. total_hours = SUM(hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes)/60, billable_hours = SUM(CASE WHEN billable=true THEN duration_minutes ELSE 0 END)/60, non_billable_hours = total_hours - billable_hours. Joins hrm_projects to hrm_timelogs on hrm_project_id, filters by date range and deleted_at IS NULL, groups by project id.

IHrmWeeklySummaryReport.ITopProject.description:
Top project entry in weekly summary report containing project identification and time tracking metrics.

This type represents a single project's contribution to the weekly time tracking report. It includes all standard project identification fields plus computed hours metrics showing how much time was logged against this project during the reporting week.

**Project Identification**

Includes id, name, color_code, status, and organization from the IHrmProject.ISummary schema for project identification and organizational context. Optional fields description, start_date, and end_date provide additional project details.

**Hours Breakdown**

The hours_breakdown object contains computed time metrics aggregated from hrm_timelogs:
- total_hours: Sum of all timelog durations (in hours) for this project during the week
- billable_hours: Sum of billable timelog durations (in hours) for this project
- non_billable_hours: Difference between total_hours and billable_hours

**Usage**

IHrmTimesheetTimelog.ITimelogUpdate.description:
Request body for updating timelog associations in a draft timesheet.

This DTO specifies which timelog UUIDs to add and remove from a draft timesheet before submission. The operation allows employees to customize which time entries are included in their weekly timesheet.

**Workflow Context**

Timesheets progress through states: draft → submitted → approved/rejected. Only draft timesheets can be modified via this endpoint. Once submitted, timelogs are locked. Once approved, timelogs are permanently locked and cannot be changed.

**Validation Rules**

- All referenced timelogs must belong to the authenticated employee
- All timelog dates must fall within the timesheet's week_start_date to week_end_date range
- Timelogs already associated with the timesheet are not duplicated when added
- Timelogs included in submitted or approved timesheets cannot be removed

**Usage**

Send this request body to PUT /hrm/member/timesheets/{timesheetId}/timelogs to modify a draft timesheet's timelog associations. The response returns the updated timesheet with recalculated total_hours.
IHrmTimesheetTimelog.ITimelogUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for PUT /hrm/member/timesheets/{timesheetId}/timelogs endpoint. This DTO does not map to a database table directly - it specifies which timelog UUIDs to add and remove from the hrm_timesheet_timelogs junction table. Backend validates: (1) timesheet exists and belongs to authenticated employee, (2) timesheet status is 'draft', (3) all timelog IDs in add_timelog_ids exist, belong to the same employee, and fall within the timesheet week period, (4) all timelog IDs in remove_timelog_ids exist, belong to the same employee, and are not locked by submitted/approved timesheets. On success, inserts rows into hrm_timesheet_timelogs for additions, soft-deletes rows (deleted_at = now) for removals, recalculates timesheet.total_hours, and returns updated IHrmTimesheet.

IHrmTimesheetTimelog.ISummary.description:
Weekly timesheet summary record for list displays with approval workflow tracking.

Provides essential timesheet information optimized for list views, including the weekly period, current workflow status, total hours logged, and employee reference. Full details including individual timelog entries are available via the detail endpoint.

**Workflow States**

- `draft`: Initial state where employees can modify included timelogs
- `submitted`: Awaiting manager review, timelogs are locked
- `approved`: Manager has approved, timelogs are permanently locked
- `rejected`: Manager returned to employee for correction, returns to draft status

**Weekly Period**

The timesheet covers a Monday-to-Sunday week defined by `week_start_date` (Monday) and `week_end_date` (Sunday). This prevents duplicate submissions for the same week.

**Key Fields**

- `total_hours`: Aggregated sum of all timelog durations included in this timesheet
- `employee`: The employee who owns this timesheet (required)
- `reviewer`: The manager who reviewed and approved or rejected (null for draft/submitted)
- `rejection_reason`: Manager's explanation when timesheet is rejected

status.description:
Current workflow state of the timesheet.

Controls the timesheet's position in the approval workflow and determines which operations are allowed. This field accepts string values representing the current state.

**Allowed Values**

- `draft`: Initial state where timelogs can be modified and added/removed
- `submitted`: Awaiting manager review, timelogs are locked from modification
- `approved`: Manager has approved, timelogs are permanently locked for audit integrity
- `rejected`: Manager returned to employee for correction, returns to draft state

**Workflow Constraints**

Only timesheets in draft status can be updated through this endpoint. Once submitted, approved, or rejected, the timesheet cannot be modified directly (except for returning to draft when rejected). Status transitions follow strict rules: draft→submitted, draft→rejected. Approved timesheets cannot be reverted to draft.

**Business Rules**

- Cannot update a timesheet that is not in draft status (returns 409 Conflict)
- Setting status to rejected requires providing a rejection_reason
- Setting status to submitted sets submitted_at timestamp automatically

Business rule: only draft timesheets can be updated. Valid transitions: draft→submitted, draft→rejected.

rejection_reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_timesheets.rejection_reason. Nullable string field, required when status is set to 'rejected'. Business rule: timesheets cannot be rejected without providing a reason. All Update DTO fields optional for partial updates.
rejection_reason.description:
Reason provided when a timesheet is rejected by a manager.

Required field when status is set to 'rejected'. Explains to the employee what corrections are needed before resubmission. Null for non-rejected statuses (draft, submitted, approved).

**Business Rules**

- Must be provided (non-null, non-empty) when status is set to 'rejected'
- Can be null or omitted when status is not 'rejected'
- Free-form text field with no length restrictions

**Usage**

When a manager rejects a timesheet, they must provide a clear explanation of what needs to be corrected. This reason is visible to the employee when the timesheet returns to draft status, guiding them on how to fix the issues before resubmitting.

IHrmTimesheetTimelog.IUpdate.description:
Timesheet update request payload for modifying week period dates and workflow status.

This DTO is used to update editable fields on a timesheet record. All fields are optional to support partial updates, allowing clients to modify only specific properties without providing the entire timesheet state.

**Workflow Constraints**

Only timesheets in draft status can be updated. Once submitted for approval, a timesheet becomes locked until a manager approves or rejects it. Approved timesheets permanently lock all included timelogs for audit integrity. Rejected timesheets return to draft status and can be updated again.

**Week Period Validation**

The week_start_date must be a Monday, and week_end_date must be exactly 6 days after week_start_date (Sunday). An employee can have at most one timesheet per week in submitted or approved status. Attempting to update to a week period that conflicts with an existing submitted or approved timesheet will result in a 409 Conflict error.

**Status Transitions**

Valid status transitions: draft → submitted, draft → rejected. When setting status to rejected, the rejection_reason field is required and must contain a non-empty string explaining why the timesheet was returned for correction.

**Excluded Fields**

The following fields are not included in this update DTO: id (auto-generated), total_hours (computed from timelogs), submitted_at/reviewed_at/created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed timestamps), hrm_employee_id/reviewed_by (foreign keys resolved from JWT context), employee/reviewer (relations), and timesheetTimelogs (composition managed via separate endpoint).

IHrmTimesheetTimelog.description:
Weekly timesheet record with approval workflow tracking employee time entries.

A timesheet represents a week of work (Monday to Sunday) and transitions through draft, submitted, approved, or rejected states. Employees create draft timesheets that automatically include all timelogs for the week, submit them for review, and receive approval or rejection from managers. Approved timesheets lock all included timelogs to prevent modifications, while rejected timesheets return to draft status for correction.

**Workflow States**

- `draft`: Initial state, timelogs can be modified
- `submitted`: Awaiting review, timelogs locked
- `approved`: Reviewed and approved, timelogs permanently locked
- `rejected`: Returned to employee for correction, returns to draft state

**Week Period**

The timesheet covers a weekly period defined by week_start_date (Monday) and week_end_date (Sunday). The week_end_date is calculated as week_start_date + 6 days.

**Review Information**

When a timesheet is approved or rejected, the reviewer field contains the reviewer's member ID, reviewed_at contains the review timestamp, and rejection_reason contains the explanation if rejected.
IHrmTimesheetTimelog.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_timesheets table with JOINs for relations. Columns: id, week_start_date, week_end_date, status, total_hours, submitted_at, reviewed_at, rejection_reason, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. FK columns hrm_employee_id and reviewed_by exposed as relation objects via JOIN: employee (JOIN hrm_employees, required), reviewer (LEFT JOIN hrm_members, nullable). Timelogs array computed via hrm_timesheet_timelogs junction table with JOIN to hrm_timelogs. Business rules: status transitions (draft→submitted→approved/rejected), week period is Monday to Sunday, total_hours calculated from timelog durations, approved timesheets lock timelogs permanently.

total_hours.description:
Total hours logged for this project during the reporting week.

Computed as the sum of all timelog durations (in minutes) divided by 60. Includes both billable and non-billable time entries.

**Computation**

Sum of hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes for all timelogs belonging to this project within the week range, converted from minutes to hours.
total_hours.x-autobe-specification: Computed as SUM(hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes)/60 where hrm_timelogs.hrm_project_id matches the project and hrm_timelogs.date falls within the reporting week. Includes both billable and non-billable time entries.

billable_hours.description:
Billable hours logged for this project during the reporting week.

Computed as the sum of timelog durations where billable=true (in minutes) divided by 60. Represents chargeable work time.

**Computation**

Sum of hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes for all billable timelogs (hrm_timelogs.billable = true) belonging to this project within the week range, converted from minutes to hours.
billable_hours.x-autobe-specification: Computed as SUM(CASE WHEN hrm_timelogs.billable = true THEN hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes ELSE 0 END)/60 where hrm_timelogs.hrm_project_id matches the project and hrm_timelogs.date falls within the reporting week. Only includes timelogs marked as billable.

non_billable_hours.description:
Non-billable hours logged for this project during the reporting week.

Computed as total_hours minus billable_hours. Represents internal work, training, meetings, or other non-chargeable activities.

**Computation**

Derived by subtracting billable_hours from total_hours. This captures all time entries marked as non-billable (hrm_timelogs.billable = false) for this project within the week range.
non_billable_hours.x-autobe-specification: Computed as total_hours minus billable_hours. Represents the portion of time that is not chargeable to clients.

IHrmWeeklySummaryReportHoursBreakdown.description:
Hours breakdown metrics for a project in weekly time tracking summary.

This type represents aggregated time tracking data computed from individual timelog entries. It provides three key metrics showing how time was allocated across billable and non-billable work for a specific project during a reporting week.

**Metrics**

- total_hours: Sum of all timelog durations for this project during the week (in hours)
- billable_hours: Sum of billable timelog durations for this project (in hours)
- non_billable_hours: Difference between total_hours and billable_hours, representing internal or non-chargeable work

**Usage**

Used in IHrmWeeklySummaryReport.ITopProject to show time distribution for top projects ranked by total hours logged. All three metrics are always present and computed together from the same timelog dataset.
IHrmWeeklySummaryReportHoursBreakdown.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation type for time tracking hours metrics. All values derived from hrm_timelogs table for a specific project during a reporting week. Computation formulas: total_hours = SUM(hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes)/60, billable_hours = SUM(CASE WHEN hrm_timelogs.billable = true THEN hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes ELSE 0 END)/60, non_billable_hours = total_hours - billable_hours. Query filters: hrm_timelogs.date within week range, hrm_timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL, hrm_timelogs.hrm_project_id matches project. All values rounded to reasonable precision for display.
